key_insight: Zero-shot compositional action models often succeed by relying on object cues instead of true verb understanding — an overlooked ‘object-driven verb shortcut’ caused by sparse/skewed compositional supervision and asymmetric learning difficulty between verbs and objects.
problem_solved: Identifies and mitigates the failure mode where models use object identity as a shortcut to predict verbs, which breaks generalization to unseen verb-object combinations.
method: Systematic diagnosis: quantify shortcutting via analyses of supervision sparsity, class skew, and asymmetric learning dynamics between verbs and objects.

Mitigation strategies: introduce targeted interventions (e.g., reweighting, regularization, representation disentangling or contrastive objectives, and data augmentation/occlusion) to reduce object-driven bias and encourage verb-focused learning.
Evaluation: test interventions in zero-shot compositional splits to verify improved compositional generalization (controlled comparisons against baseline ZS-CAR models).
impact: Highlights a concrete, actionable failure mode and provides practical mitigation patterns so practitioners can build more robust compositional action recognizers that truly learn verbs independent of object identity.
visual_elements: Sankey or flow diagram showing how object cues dominate predictions (object → predicted verb) versus desired verb-driven composition (verb + object → action).
Bar chart of supervision sparsity/skewness (frequency of seen verb-object pairs) and its correlation with shortcutting rate.
Before/after examples: video frames with model attention or saliency maps showing object-focused vs verb-focused attention.
Pipeline graphic summarizing diagnosis → mitigation → evaluation steps
paper_title: Why Can't I Open My Drawer? Mitigating Object-Driven Shortcuts in Zero-Shot Compositional Action Recognition
paper_authors: Geo Ahn, Inwoong Lee, Taeoh Kim, Minho Shim, Dongyoon Wee
